diffs.diff: header pin 2: part says RXD, datasheet reading says RXD/SDA
diffs.evidence: Benewake datasheet SJ-GU-TFmini Plus-01 A04, pin table: "(2) White PIN-2 RXD/SDA Receiving/Data". Same physical pin (pin 2, white wire) in the same position; SDA is only its function after the sensor is switched to I2C mode with command 5A 05 0A 01. Table 5: "Communication interface: UART, I2C and I/O - Factory setting: UART". The part models the factory UART mode only (interface uart, 115200 8N1), so RXD is the correct name for how this model wires and drives it; no wiring difference.

diffs.diff: header pin 3: part says TXD, datasheet reading says TXD/SCL/IO
diffs.evidence: Benewake datasheet SJ-GU-TFmini Plus-01 A04, pin table: "(3) Blue/Green PIN-3 TXD/SCL/IO Transmitting/Clock/IO". Same physical pin (pin 3, blue wire); SCL and IO are alternate functions only in I2C or I/O switching mode, which must be configured by command. Factory setting (Table 5) is UART, which is the mode this part models, so TXD (sensor output -> board RX) is correct; no wiring difference.

diffs.diff: distance_cm: datasheet reading gives 1 per count, the part's model has none
diffs.evidence: Product manual 5.4: "Dist(Distance): Represents the output of the distance value detected by TFmini Plus, with the unit in cm by default. This value is interpreted into the decimal value in the range of 0-1200." The part's model already uses exactly 1 cm per count: sim.uartStream bytes 2-3 are {control: value, bits 16, scale 1, littleEndian} with unit cm, and the driver computes dist = f[2] | (f[3] << 8) in cm. The gate reports 'none' only because it reads conversions from sim.measure/responses, not from uartStream; there is no disagreement in value.
